LanguageData.RimForex_Loan1Desc: Underwritten by biological assets; future bodily use-rights are accepted as collateral. Interest floats with your heart rate; freshness sets your credit line. Overdue fees are settled as surgical scheduling.
LanguageData.RimForex_Loan2Desc: Community mutual aid: low interest, high breeding. Membership requirements are loose, repayment requirements are loose, and growth in member count is arranged separately. Assimilation is far more efficient than repayment.
LanguageData.RimForex_Loan3Desc: Emergency liquidity for colonists short on cash. Collateral accepted: silver, components, bio-appendages. Our overdue process is streamlined: we repossess the leg you would need to run with, and you keep the rest.

LanguageData.RimForex_GuideIntro: FX trading is three things: pick a direction, add leverage, don't get wiped out. These five short sections cover the rest.
LanguageData.RimForex_GuideLong:
Going long means buying: you're betting the rate goes up.
What makes it go up? · News: a faction wins a war or its economy improves, and its currency usually rises. · Price action: after a long slide, a turn back up is often the reversal.
Profit = units × the rise. Higher is better; if it falls, you lose.
LanguageData.RimForex_GuideShort:
Going short means selling first and buying back later: you're betting the rate goes down.
What makes it fall? · The faction just lost a war, its economy collapsed, or its currency is being dumped. · A long rally that has stalled.
Profit = units × the fall. Mind the direction: if the rate rises, a short loses.
LanguageData.RimForex_GuideLiquidation:
Leverage magnifies profits and losses alike.
· At 45% margin health the terminal warns you and pauses the game; you can add margin. · At 30% the position is closed for you — that's a margin call. · If a gap jumps past the stop-out line, losses exceed your margin and the balance goes negative — that's a blow-up. You cannot open positions or withdraw until you deposit silver.
The higher the leverage, the closer the stop-out: at 100x, a 0.7% move against you is enough.
LanguageData.RimForex_GuideCandle:
Each candle records four prices over a period: open, high, low, close.
· Body: the distance from open to close. Green when it rose, red when it fell. · Wicks: the thin lines above and below, marking the high and low reached.
Long wicks mean price pushed and got pushed back — buyers and sellers are fighting.
Candles describe what already happened. They do not predict the future.
LanguageData.RimForex_GuideProfit:
First, the honest part: there is no sure-win strategy. Get the direction wrong and you lose, at any leverage.
Three habits that improve your odds:
1. Start with low leverage. 1-5x survives normal swings; 100x dies to one bad quote. 2. Don't churn. You pay the spread and fees every round trip. 3. Watch the news. War and crash expectations beat staring at candles.
Also remember: open positions cost overnight interest, and loans cost loan interest — the longer you hold, the more you pay.
LanguageData.RimForex_GuideLoan:
With the terminal selected, the "Official lending service" gizmo offers four lenders with different rates and terms.
Borrowed silver is debt, not income. If it isn't cleared by the term, the debt is charged to your balance and can push it negative.
LanguageData.RimForex_GuideGlossary: Margin: the silver you post. Notional: margin × leverage. Spread: the gap between buy and sell price, paid on open and close. Fee: 0.02% per trade, minimum 2 silver. Stop-out line: forced close at 30% margin health. Margin call: being forcibly closed. Blow-up: losses exceed margin, balance goes negative. Lock-in: you must cross one quote before you can close.
